blocks.text: Mastering Slack navigation on your Mac

As a content moderator, you cannot afford to waste time clicking through menus. Your Mac is a powerful tool when you use the right keyboard shortcuts. Start by pressing Command (⌘) + K to open the Quick Switcher. This lets you jump to any channel or direct message by typing the first few letters of the name. It is the fastest way to move between your team channel and your lead coordinator.

If you are struggling to find a specific policy update, use the search bar. Press Command (⌘) + G to open the general search. Use modifiers like from: to narrow results by user or in: to look within a specific channel. This saves you from scrolling through hundreds of messages.

High-volume moderation requires intense focus. If constant pings distract you, use the built-in notification schedules. Click your profile photo, go to Preferences, and select Notifications. Set a schedule that matches your shift hours. You can also use the /dnd command in any channel to pause alerts for a specific amount of time.

If you miss an important alert, check your settings to ensure they are not being blocked by macOS system permissions. Go to System Settings > Notifications > Slack on your Mac to verify that alerts are set to show in the Notification Center.

Slack can consume a lot of memory on a Mac, especially if you monitor many active channels. If you notice the app lagging, clear your cache. Go to the Help menu at the top of your screen, select Troubleshooting, and then click Clear Cache and Restart. This often resolves performance issues without losing your message history.

Keep your app updated. Slack requires macOS 14 Sonoma or later for the latest features. Check for updates by going to the Slack menu > Check for Updates. Staying on the latest version, currently in the 4.53.x series, ensures you have the latest security patches and performance improvements.

When you report an incident to your team, use Slack formatting to make it readable. Use Command (⌘) + B for bold text to highlight key policy violations. Use Shift + Enter to create a new line within a message without sending it. This is useful when you need to list multiple pieces of evidence or provide a structured explanation for a decision.

faq.question: How do I jump between channels quickly?
faq.answer: Press Command (⌘) + K to open the Quick Switcher, then type the channel name and press Enter.

faq.question: Why is Slack slow on my Mac?
faq.answer: It may be a cache issue. Go to Help > Troubleshooting > Clear Cache and Restart to refresh the app.

faq.question: Can I use voice to draft messages?
faq.answer: Yes. Hold the fn key on your Mac to dictate text directly into the Slack input field.
